names.name: Arlington Hotel (first building)
names.operator: Samuel W. Fordyce and two other investors
names.note: First luxury hotel in Hot Springs; rebuilt 1892-93

names.name: Arlington Hotel (current building, now Arlington Resort Hotel & Spa)
names.operator: not found for the casino era; Sky Capitol Group per Wikipedia (2023)
names.note: Mann and Stern design; renovation under way 2023

label.basis: Kefauver hearings show Adonis and others as hotel guests and a witness calling it a bath-town hotel, but no page shows the Arlington ran a casino, or Madden or Binion held an interest.

venues.corrections: Closed 1967 is not supported: the hotel was never a 1967 closure (current building 1924, still operating). 'Kefauver Committee named it a mob-controlled casino' is not supported; Kefauver pages only record guests. Madden's Hot Springs gambling is tied to the Southern Club/Hotel Arkansas, and no opened source ties Binion to the Arlington.

label.basis: I could not open any page about the Ohio Club; the Kefauver parts searched do not name it.

venues.corrections: Opening 1905 and closing 1967 not confirmed; the 1967 closure of casinos generally is sourced.

names.name: Southern Club
names.operator: William Stokley Jacobs held a stake (died 1940); Owney Madden reported to have held control; later operators not found
names.note: Reopened under McLaughlin's machine; casino still operating in 1959; closed in 1967 crackdown (all Hot Springs casinos)

label.basis: Wikipedia and a 1959 Variety report describe a casino run with official tolerance and Madden-linked nightlife, but no court record, commission finding or Kefauver passage naming the Southern Club was opened.

venues.corrections: 'Chicago Outfit backing' and '1960s raids documented' not found in opened sources; the 1959 Variety piece says operators paid weekly fines and were not raided. Opening 1920 not confirmed; reopening under McLaughlin was after 1927. Label 'documented' is not supported; use 'alleged'.

label.basis: No page about the Vapors was opened; the searched Kefauver parts do not mention it.

venues.corrections: 'Listed in Kefauver Committee exhibits' not confirmed: no hit for Vapors in the 19 hearing volumes searched (text search of OCR).

names.name: Lookout House (Lookout House, Inc.; casino run as the Lookout Club)
names.operator: Cleveland partners named in hearing (Kleinman, Dalitz, Tucker, Rothkopf) per witnesses; by mid-1951 Brink, Carr brothers and others
names.note: Gambling reported stopped in early 1951 after grand jury action; later closing not found

label.basis: Congressional hearing record (Kefauver Parts 6 and 15) has sworn testimony that the Lookout Club ran the casino with Cleveland partners.

venues.corrections: Closing 1961 and 'FBI surveillance confirmed' not confirmed; hearings show gambling stopped in early 1951. Opening 1927 not confirmed.

names.name: Glenn Rendezvous
names.operator: Pete Schmidt, then Levinson brothers and Arthur Dennert from 1948
names.note: Remodeled 1943; sold 1948; named in 1951 hearing as a Dennert gambling place

label.basis: Kefauver Part 15 names it as an illegal gambling place run by Dennert; the Levinson link comes from Wikipedia, and no opened page ties it to Cleveland.

venues.corrections: 'Operated by Cleveland family associates' is not supported: sources show Newport operators Dennert and the Levinsons. Opening 1930 is not supported (Rendezvous name 1943). 'IRS and FBI files' not found.

names.name: Colonial Inn
names.operator: Frank Erickson, Joe Adonis (Doto, 15%), B. Briggs and others per tax return; earlier Ben Marden/Lou Walters per other (unopened) sources

names.name: Minsky's Burlesque
names.note: Colonial Inn building later used as a burlesque house; casino operations moved to Club Boheme

label.basis: Kefauver Part 1 reads the Colonial Inn tax return into the record showing Joe Adonis (Doto) 15 percent and Erickson and Briggs as owners.

venues.corrections: Closing year 1957 is wrong for the casino: the hearing says it operated through 1948. 'Chicago Outfit ran it' not shown; owners named are Erickson, Adonis and Briggs. Opening 1935 not confirmed.

names.name: Beverly Hills Country Club (casino: Country Club Enterprise)
names.operator: Pete Schmidt (founder, per Wikipedia); Cleveland group Dalitz, Kleinman, Tucker and others in 1951 record
names.note: Gambling on the site from 1926 per Wikipedia; sold 1967

names.name: Beverly Hills Supper Club
names.operator: Joseph Cole, Sam Klein, Carl Glickman and others; Schilling family from 1974
names.note: Destroyed by the 28 May 1977 fire (165 deaths)

label.basis: Kefauver Part 6 has sworn testimony and records showing a casino operation at Beverly Hills with Cleveland partners.

venues.corrections: Shondor Birns is not named in the pages opened; the partners named are Kleinman, Dalitz, Tucker, Rothkopf and others. Closed 1961 is not supported: the property continued to 1977 (fire). Location is Southgate, not Newport.

names.name: Balinese Room
names.operator: Maceo brothers; Fertitta family from c.1954 per Wikipedia (Maceo page)
names.note: Rangers raids after 1956; casino ended 1957; reopened 2001 without casino; destroyed by Hurricane Ike 2008

label.basis: Wikipedia-based histories say it was a well-known illegal casino of the Maceos but no conviction or commission finding was found; the Kefauver part opened only names it as a customer.

venues.corrections: Opened 1942 is a renaming; the site opened 1929 as Maceo's Grotto. 'Closed 1957' is the end of gambling after state action, but the club reopened 2001 without a casino and was destroyed in 2008. Texas Ranger primary sources not opened.

gaps: Encyclopedia of Arkansas, TSHA entries, Northern Kentucky news sites and the Mob Museum refused scripted access (403/Cloudflare/DNS); no state archive or court opinions were opened for Hot Springs.
Ohio Club and Vapors Club: no page opened; labels unsupported.
Lookout House, Glenn Rendezvous, Beverly Hills: closing dates not found.
Texas Ranger / state-probe primary sources on the Balinese Room not opened (recalled, not fetched: Texas Ranger Hall of Fame Klevenhagen article cited by Wikipedia).
Hot Springs: Kefauver searches were by OCR text on 19 volumes; the Third Interim Report was not opened.
